stories.headline: Telangana SIR: ‘Not one illegal immigrant found on Hyderabad district’s electoral rolls’
stories.bodyText:
The Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls (SIR) in Telangana has failed to detect even one illegal immigrant registered in the voters lists of the Hyderabad district’s 15 constituencies.
District Election Officer and Commissioner of Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) R.V. Karnan has confirmed this, and said only a few Nepali citizens were found on the rolls, and they stand deleted.
“Though foreign nationals, we cannot call them illegal immigrants, as they have entered the country through legal route. But since they do not have citizenship here and hold their franchise back in Nepal, their inclusion in electoral rolls here is illegal, and we have removed their names,” Mr. Karnan said.
While exact number of such immigrants is not yet available, Mr. Karnan said 10 to 12 people were detected on the rolls of the Sanath Nagar Constituency. He categorically denied presence of Bangladesh nationals or Rohingya Muslims on the electoral rolls of Hyderabad district.
This trumps the narrative that illegal infiltrators into the city from Myanmar and Bangladesh have enrolled themselves as voters in the electoral rolls over the years compromising the sanctity of electoral process.
On November 2, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on his visit to the city, claimed that the SIR process has eliminated three crore illegal infiltrators from the electoral rolls.
The SIR 2026 has been designed with an additional component of mapping the voters with 2002 electoral rolls, with the express purpose of sifting out the infiltrators and ineligible persons from the voters list.
The electors were to fill in their details as they existed in the 2002 voters list, in order to prove their citizenship. Notices for appearance with documents to prove citizenship were issued to 32,36,659 electors who were declared as ‘unmapped’ though a large number of them had mapped themselves with 2002 rolls. Glitches in the ECINET software were cited as the reason for the mapping details not being uploaded onto the app.

stories.headline: Democratic gains mount in U.S. midterms as Donald Trump faces bruising verdict
stories.deck: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night
stories.bodyText:
Democrats notched a string of early victories in U.S. midterm elections Tuesday, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat and making inroads in conservative House districts as President Donald Trump faced the prospect of a bruising election setback.
The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night.
The vote was a nationwide judgment on Mr. Trump’s turbulent second term, with discontent over living costs, tariffs and the U.S. war against Iran — which has driven fuel prices sharply higher — weighing on the president and his party.
Alarm bells went off early for Republicans as counting started.
Democrats captured a Republican-held House seat in North Carolina, in a district Mr. Trump won comfortably in 2024, while several contests in Florida suggested that redrawn electoral boundaries might not deliver the gains Republicans had hoped for.
Although control of Congress remained undecided, those results raised the possibility of a wider Democratic advance into territory normally considered safe for Trump’s party.
In a further blow to Republicans, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms was projected to win Georgia’s governorship, becoming the nation’s first Black woman Governor and ending 24 years of Republican rule.
There were important Republican victories, however.
In Florida, Trump-backed Byron Donalds won the governor’s race, becoming the state’s first Black governor, while Republican Ashley Moody retained a US Senate seat.
Senate breakthrough
Democrat Roy Cooper, a popular former North Carolina governor, delivered one of the night’s most consequential results by defeating Michael Whatley, the former Republican National Committee chairman handpicked by Mr. Trump.
North Carolina has voted for Mr. Trump three times, but Cooper campaigned on a pledge to lower living costs and will replace retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who had clashed with the president.
In Georgia, Senator Jon Ossoff, a rising Democratic figure seen as a potential 2028 presidential contender, defeated his Republican challenger and preserved a seat the party needed to defend.
Democrats also held an open Senate seat in New Hampshire, where Chris Pappas won election to become the first openly gay man to serve in the chamber.
Republicans began the night with 53 of the Senate’s 100 seats, leaving Democrats needing a net gain of four for control. All 435 House seats were contested, with Democrats needing to flip just three.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries told reporters the country was “on the brink of a dramatic change of direction.”
Trump faces constraints
If Democrats capture the House, they could block Trump’s legislative plans and use congressional committees to investigate his administration over the Iran war, deportations and alleged corruption.
A Senate takeover would go further, allowing them to block judicial nominees and senior administration appointments, fundamentally changing Mr. Trump’s ability to govern during the final two years of his presidency.
For voters, the fight was often about the cost of everyday life.
“Rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes keep climbing, and I want people in Congress who will actually do something about costs,” 24-year-old Los Angeles voter Taylor Cook told AFP.
Mr. Trump defended his record in a final television appearance on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), praising his tariffs, immigration crackdown and military campaign against Iran.
“We have to keep America great. We’re great now. We were terrible two years ago,” the 80-year-old told Fox News.
Reflecting Trump’s rhetoric, Republican voter Maru Restrepo, 70, told AFP in Miami that Democrats had become “very socialist,” reflecting the fierce ideological divisions of the campaign.
Uncertainty remained over whether Trump would accept an unfavorable result. He has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims of election fraud and tried to overturn his 2020 presidential defeat.
“I veto everything,” Trump said in a podcast released Monday, contemplating the possibility of a Democratic Congress before adding that he might eventually negotiate deals.
Published - November 04, 2026 08:40 am IST

stories.headline: US elections: K Bottoms makes history as first Black woman governor, flips Georgia seat
stories.deck: Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia after defeating Rick Jackson in the recent election. Her victory signifies a historic moment as she becomes the first Black woman to hold this position. Bottoms focused her campaign on economic issues, pledging to expand Medicaid and raise the minimum wage. Jackson's significant campaign spending did not prevent his defeat despite his…
stories.bodyText:
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman to hold the office after defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Tuesday's election, the Associated Press reported.
Her victory also marks the first time a Democrat has won the state's gubernatorial race since 1998.
A former mayor of Atlanta, Bottoms won despite a significant campaign spending disadvantage, with Jackson having spent more than $200 million of his personal fortune on his campaign. She will succeed Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who was barred by law from seeking a third term.
Bottoms' victory also marks a shift in a state where voters have historically been reluctant to elect candidates from Atlanta to the governor's office.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
According to news agency AP, the growth of Georgia's largest metropolitan area has been reshaping the state's political landscape.
Bottoms focused campaign on economy and policy
Although her election breaks a historic barrier, Bottoms largely focused her campaign on economic issues and her policy proposals rather than the significance of her candidacy.
The descendant of enslaved Georgians, she has spoken about her family's history in the state and her grandfather's move from rural Georgia to Atlanta.
“I am at least a fifth-generation Georgian,” she said. “I say ‘at least’ because we can only trace our family back five generations — to a plantation in Crawfordville.”
She also recalled how her grandfather had to “walk through these back doors” of downtown buildings that she would later enter through the front as Atlanta's mayor. She said her ancestry “is always present with me”.
On policy, Bottoms called for expanding Medicaid to cover hundreds of thousands more people and raising Georgia's minimum wage to $15 an hour. She also pledged to increase pay for teachers, firefighters, police officers and other public employees.
Her proposals included pausing new data centre developments, stopping the installation of additional automated Flock cameras used by law enforcement, and repealing Georgia's ban on abortions after the sixth week of pregnancy.
“This is a life and death issue,” she said of the abortion restrictions, citing cases of women dying from miscarriages and pregnancy complications because doctors feared criminal prosecution under the law.
Bottoms also pledged to “make sure we are protected from the harmful policies of Donald Trump”.
During the campaign, she repeatedly contrasted her approach with Jackson's stated ambition to govern like “Trump with a Southern tone” and become the president's “favorite governor”.
“I’m not running to be his favorite governor,” Bottoms said during the rivals' only debate. “I’m running to work on behalf of people like you.”
Jackson's spending and attacks fail to prevent defeat
Jackson, a businessman who founded Jackson Healthcare, entered the governor's race as a relatively unknown candidate but used his personal wealth and outsider appeal to secure the Republican nomination.
He had defeated the sitting lieutenant governor, who had received Trump's early endorsement, as well as the state attorney general and secretary of state.
During the general election campaign, Jackson attacked Bottoms' record as Atlanta mayor. His television advertisements featured footage of protests following the 2020 police killings of Rayshard Brooks in Atlanta and George Floyd in Minneapolis. He also criticised Bottoms for not seeking a second term as mayor, accusing her of abandoning the city.
Bottoms, in turn, questioned Jackson's claims that he understood the economic difficulties faced by ordinary Georgians. She pointed to his company's government contracts and accused him of using money earned from taxpayers to try to “buy this election”.
Georgia's political landscape faces a new test
Bottoms' election comes as Georgia has increasingly become a two-party battleground. Democrats have won three US Senate elections in the state since Trump's first presidential victory a decade ago.
The state also re-elected Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff on Tuesday. He will serve alongside Raphael Warnock, Georgia's first Black senator. Ossoff is also the state's first Jewish senator.
Bottoms' victory follows three consecutive Georgia gubernatorial elections in which a Black woman led the Democratic ticket. Republican Kemp defeated Stacey Abrams in the previous two contests. Abrams, a prominent voting rights advocate and Democratic fundraiser, did not seek the nomination for a third run.
Bottoms was among eight Black major-party nominees for governor on Tuesday's ballot. There have been only three Black governors elected in US history, all Democratic men.
This year, Bottoms and Republican Lisa Demuth of Minnesota were both seeking to become the first Black women elected governor of their respective states.
Republicans have controlled Georgia's governorship and both chambers of its General Assembly for more than two decades.
Democrats were seeking to flip the state House in Tuesday's elections, while Republicans were expected to retain their Senate majority, leaving Bottoms potentially having to work with at least one Republican-controlled chamber.

stories.headline: US polls: Indian-American candidates script key wins; Khanna, Bera await verdict
stories.bodyText:
The 2026 US midterm elections are witnessing a growing presence of Indian-American candidates in American politics, with several securing victories in key congressional and state-level contests.
Democrat Pia Dandiya won election to the US House of Representatives from Florida's 22nd Congressional District, defeating Republican Casey Askar.
Indian-American Democrat 
Suhas Subramanyam
 also secured re-election from Virginia's 10th Congressional District, while Maryland Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller won another term alongside Democratic Governor Wes Moore.
The victories mark early successes for Indian-origin candidates as several other closely watched races remain undecided. 
US Midterm Election Results 2026
The midterm results could reshape the balance of power in Congress and influence the political direction of both parties ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
Pia Dandiya wins Florida's 22nd Congressional District
Democrat Pia Dandiya won election to the US House of Representatives from Florida's 22nd Congressional District, defeating Republican candidate Casey Askar.
Her victory marks a Democratic win in a newly redrawn district following Florida Governor Ron DeSantis' congressional redistricting effort ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. 
The district stretches from Palm Beach County through parts of Broward and Hendry counties, across the Everglades and west to Marco Island in Collier County.
Dandiya, a former teacher and high school principal in Harlem, previously served as a White House Fellow and worked at Apple. Born and raised in Palm Beach County to Indian immigrant parents, she made education, affordability and economic opportunity central to her campaign.
Her Republican opponent, Askar, is a Naples-based businessman and Marine Corps veteran who built his career in restaurant franchising. He campaigned as a supporter of President Donald Trump and his administration's policies.
The contest attracted attention after Florida lawmakers approved a new congressional map in May 2026, significantly reshaping District 22 and creating an open-seat race. Dandiya secured the Democratic nomination in August, defeating attorney Kaysia Earley, while Askar emerged from a crowded Republican primary.
Suhas Subramanyam secures re-election in Virginia
Indian-American Democrat Suhas Subramanyam won re-election to the US House of Representatives from Virginia's 10th Congressional District, defeating Republican challenger Dave T Beckwith.
Subramanyam secured 63.16 per cent of the vote, polling 1,73,106 votes, while Beckwith received 34.66 per cent, or 94,990 votes. Independent candidate Ahsen Mujeeb Malik finished third with 1.99 per cent (5,444 votes), while write-in candidates accounted for the remaining 0.19 per cent.
The victory comes after Subramanyam urged Indian-Americans to participate actively in the midterm elections, saying their votes and voices mattered more than ever amid rising hate and discrimination in the US.
Speaking to news agency ANI after casting his vote at a polling station in Manassas, Virginia, on Tuesday, he said the state was witnessing record turnout and expressed confidence about the Democrats' prospects.
"Well, come out and vote. Make your voice heard. Your vote matters more than ever, especially at a time when we're seeing record hate in our community, in our country," he said.
Encouraging Indian-Americans to enter politics, Subramanyam referred to his own electoral journey, saying, "I ran for office and I won. You can too. If you want to get involved in the political process, now is the time. It's more important than ever."
He also criticised the functioning of the US Congress, saying voters were dissatisfied with representatives who prioritised the President over ordinary citizens. He said Democrats would focus on restoring healthcare and food assistance and ensuring public resources benefited Americans.
Born in Virginia in 1979 to Indian immigrant parents, Subramanyam is the first Indian-American to represent the state's 10th Congressional District. His mother is from Bengaluru, while his father grew up in Chennai and Secunderabad.
Aruna Miller wins another term as Maryland Lieutenant Governor
In Maryland, Indian-American Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller secured another term after NBC News projected the re-election of Democratic Governor Wes Moore.
Miller, who contested alongside Moore on the Democratic ticket, defeated Republican lieutenant governor candidate Rob Krop, the running mate of former state delegate Dan Cox.
Her re-election ensures continued Indian-American representation in one of the country's highest state executive offices.
Meanwhile, the electoral fate of other Indian-American candidates, including Republican Mahesh Ganorkar in North Carolina, Democrat Ro Khanna in California, Democrat Ami Bera Democrat Pooja Sethi in Texas, remained undecided as counting and results continued.
The early victories have added to the visibility of Indian-American candidates in the midterm elections, with the results also expected to offer an indication of how voters view Trump's policies and the direction of the Republican Party.
The outcomes could further shape the debate within the Democratic Party over its political strategy ahead of 2028, with divisions persisting between those advocating a more populist economic message and those favouring a centrist approach to regain swing voters. Strong performances by candidates from either camp could strengthen their respective positions in the contest over the party's future leadership.

- November 04, 2026 03:19U.S. stocks end mostly up as markets await election results Wall Street stocks finished mostly higher as oil prices continued to pull back while markets awaited results from U.S. midterm elections that could reshape President Donald Trump’s final two years in office. - November 04, 2026 02:46Our presence makes a big difference: Georgia volunteers watch the polls Linda Jones has set up a folding chair near a polling station in Atlanta, Georgia, to watch out for anything that might keep people from casting their ballots in the U.S. midterms. “I want to help people navigate the voting, which has gotten more and more complicated,” said the septuagenarian, who is serving as an election observer for the first time. She and two other volunteers will keep a close watch on activity around this polling station, set up in a public library, and report any issues that arise. “In a climate like we are in the country, there’s misinformation, there are actions that are taken that discourage some people from voting, certain parts of the population,” she said. -AFP
- November 04, 2026 02:15Courts rebuff Trump's pressure on state election officials In the hours before polls opened for the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday, federal judges issued a series of rulings restricting the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to pressure state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting. Over the past several months, as President Donald Trump’s fellow Republicans geared up to defend their majorities in both houses of Congress, the administration ramped up a crackdown on noncitizen voting, which Mr. Trump allies say is a major problem even though evidence suggests it is exceedingly rare. That push has repeatedly encountered resistance in the courts. Federal judges have found that the Trump administration was overstepping its authority by wading into election administration, a responsibility that the U.S. Constitution assigns to the states, and that lists it had generated of alleged noncitizens registered to vote were inaccurate and risked disenfranchising naturalised U.S. citizens. -Reuters
- November 04, 2026 01:33Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in tight House race Ballot machines malfunctioned in a hotly contested House race in New York state Tuesday, prompting right-wing influencers to fling unfounded allegations of U.S. midterms voter fraud even as local election officials insisted all ballots would be counted. President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven claims about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable. The Westchester County Board of Elections said it was aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county. The board “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags, it said in a statement. -AFP

- November 04, 2026 00:15Rock star Springsteen warns against govt interference in U.S. midterms U.S. rock legend Bruce Springsteen, a staunch Democrat, urged election officials Tuesday to resist any government voting interference amid fears President Donald Trump’s administration may intervene in the midterms. “I’m speaking to election officials and representatives of our government on election day. You have sworn an oath to preserve, protect and defend our Constitution,” the 77-year-old said in a video on Instagram. “That means you have a solemn duty to ensure that our votes are securely counted,” he said. “You who represent us must never consent to any directives that undermine our constitutional right to a free and fair election.” “Our vote is our voice, and it’s up to you to ensure that our voice is heard,” added Springsteen, wearing a brown flannel shirt. -AFP
- November 04, 2026 00:14European stocks slip as West Asia uncertainty makes for caution Europe’s benchmark equities index slipped on Tuesday, as doubts over a potential West Asia peace deal kept markets on edge ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, while investors also assessed a slew of earnings. The pan-European STOXX 600 index closed 0.58% lower at 645.66 points, with mining shares leading declines on weaker copper prices. Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters. Overnight, the United States carried out what it called defensive strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island. -Reuters
- November 04, 2026 00:08How Trump could interfere in U.S. midterm elections State officials who run U.S. elections are braced for possible intervention by President Donald Trump’s administration in Tuesday’s midterms -- fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavourable results. Mr. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to keep control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to “nationalise” voting in at least 15 places. The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical. The U.S. Constitution gives the president no direct role in running elections, and courts have so far rebuffed the administration’s main legal challenges. -AFP
- November 04, 2026 00:05NASA astronaut Anil Menon, others vote from space Three NASA astronauts, including Anil Menon, on Tuesday cast their ballots in the U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station orbiting over 400 kms above Earth. Mr. Menon and two other astronauts – Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins – filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to election officials. “Yes, you can even vote from space,” Mr. Menon said in a post on X. Mr. Menon reached the International Space Station on July 14 on board a Russian Soyuz mission. Delaney and Watkins reached the orbital laboratory on October 1 on board a SpaceX rocket. “All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from Space Station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials,” Mr. Menon said. -PTI

Powders in letters tested have been determined to be either yeast or flour, the FBI said in an affidavit. -Reuters

briefs.headline: JNU to confer ‘Professor Emeritus’ title on Amitabh Mattoo
briefs.deck: After deliberations at the meeting, it was decided that the title would be conferred effective after the date of his voluntary retirement on February 28, 2027
briefs.bodyText:
The Executive Council of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) has decided to confer the title ‘Professor Emeritus’ on Amitabh Mattoo, Dean School of International Studies (SIS). He has sought voluntary retirement from the University.
Mr. Mattoo’s name was recommended by Rajesh Rajagopalan professor from SIS. After deliberations at the meeting, it was decided that title of ‘Professor Emeritus’ in JNU would be conferred effective after the date of his voluntary retirement on February 28, 2027.
Before being made Dean in 2024, Mr. Mattoo was Chair of the Centre for International Politics, Organisation and Disarmament at SIS. Also a former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jammu, he is the only Padma Shri awardee currently on the rolls of JNU.
Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Mattoo said that JNU has never been simply a place where he works but has been his intellectual home and the crucible of his ideas. “One may retire from a university’s service, but never from its embrace,” he said.
On being conferred the title, he expressed his gratitude to the university and said: “Over the years I have been fortunate in honours and in office. This one is different. It comes from an institution to which I have given a great deal of myself, and from which I have received far more.” He added that offices pass, titles fade but what remains is the affection of students, the regard of colleagues, the long companionship of ideas, and the quiet privilege of belonging.
JNU currently has 16 professors who have been conferred the title of ‘Professor Emeritus’ including Romilla Thapar, Asis Datta, Prabhat Patnaik, H.S Gill, and Zoya Hassan.
According to the guidelines or conferment of the title of ‘Professor Emeritus’ in JNU, those nominated should have made significant and distinctive contribution to the development of JNU as an institution, served JNU as Professor for at least 15 years, be a scholar of nationally and internationally recognized eminence and her/his contribution should have made a difference to the discipline and/or to the society.
The difference to the discipline/society could be judged in terms of formulation of new concepts/paradigms/hypotheses/innovations by peer group academics, nations and should be in evidence through publications and other form of research output, JNU’s guidelines say.

briefs.headline: Rising Democratic star Jon Ossoff’s reelection fuels presidential prospects
briefs.deck: While the 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for President,” his victory in Georgia bolsters his status in the Democratic Party two years before the next presidential vote
briefs.bodyText:
Jon Ossoff’s reelection on Tuesday (November 3., 2026) to the Senate in the southern state of Georgia will fuel speculation of a 2028 presidential run by one of the Democratic Party’s young rising stars.
While the 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for President,” his victory in Georgia bolsters his status in the Democratic Party two years before the next presidential vote.
NBC News and CBS News called the race in Mr. Ossoff’s favour, as he fended off a challenge from Republican Mike Collins in a state that President Donald Trump won in 2024.
The victory does not mean the Democratic Party gained a seat in the 100-member Senate, but it is nevertheless good news for the Democrats.
Some of his supporters, including 26-year-old nurse Gracie Surface, told AFP that she hopes he runs for president.
“We need him. We need some young blood,” she said after casting her vote in Atlanta, Georgia.
Mr. Ossoff, who has appeared with rolled-up shirt sleeves and a youthful vibe, has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama, who appeared on the campaign trail to support him.
Mr. Ossoff has also delivered blistering speeches criticizing Trump, attacking the president’s handling of the US war on Iran and accusing him of profiting from his office.
His comments on Trump’s loyal aide Natalie Harp, in particular, made headlines and drew Trump’s ire over the summer.
White House anger
“The President sleeps through his meetings. He golfs and trades stocks. He doesn’t want to do the job,” Mr. Ossoff told a campaign rally in August.
“He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar,” Mr. Ossoff added, referring to the 35-year-old former television news personality who has been a constant presence by Trump’s side.
His comments thrust Harp further into the spotlight, setting the internet alight -- and angering the White House.
Mr. Trump has since dismissed Mr. Ossoff as a “Pee-wee Herman lookalike,” while White House Communications Director Steven Cheung called the lawmaker “the biggest cuck loser in politics,” using internet slang for a submissive man.
Still, Mr. Ossoff’s supporters praise his authenticity and ability to transcend partisan divides to bring people together across party lines.
He shows the “sign of a true leader,” said Catherine Urbain, who works in the healthcare sector.
Obama comparisons
“When he speaks, I think of Barack Obama,” said Mary, a canvasser in her 60s who did not give her last name.
“I think it’s because he’s empathetic. He’s real,” she said.
Mr. Obama, the first Black U.S. president, remains a giant within the Democratic Party.
Others like Jan Callum, a 77-year-old retired teacher, said Mr. Ossoff is “very articulate” but added that it is difficult to compare between the politicians.
Still, Mr. Obama’s travel to rally support for Mr. Ossoff has given further substance to a comparison earlier drawn by The New York Times.
Urbain reminisced on attending a rally for former Democratic nominee Kamala Harris two years ago when Mr. Ossoff took the stage.
“When I heard him speak then, I was like: ‘This man is phenomenal. He’s going to be president,’” she recalled.
“I feel he’s authentic, he cares but also that he’s not scared to stand up,” she added. “I feel that he’s one of the few that really doesn’t let Trump get away.”
Mr. Ossoff made a major political breakthrough in 2021, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat as he won a runoff election.
At 33, he became the youngest senator for that legislative term.
Previously, he was an aide to civil rights icon John Lewis, and before entering politics, he ran a documentary film production firm, focusing particularly on corruption.
U.S. voters rejected Trump’s ‘corruption and incompetence’: Ossoff
Democrat Jon Ossoff said that victories by his party in crucial US midterm elections represent a rejection of President Donald Trump by Americans.
“In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump,” Mr. Ossoff said in an energetic speech to supporters after winning re-election in the southern state of Georgia.

briefs.headline: Pia Dandiya, first-generation Indian-American, wins U.S. House of Representatives from Florida
briefs.deck: Ms. Dandiya, a former high school principal, bagged 51.9% of the votes to become the newest Indian-American U.S. congresswoman, as per the results declared
briefs.bodyText:
Indian American Pia Dandiya won the election to the U.S. House of Representatives from Florida’s 22nd congressional district, defeating Casey Askar, a Marine veteran.
Ms. Dandiya, a former high school principal, bagged 51.9% of the votes to become the newest Indian-American U.S. congresswoman, as per the results declared on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
Her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.
Born to parents who migrated to the U.S. from India, Ms. Dandiya had earlier sought to challenge Republican Brian Mast, the chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, from Florida’s 21st district.
The former high school principal later shifted to South Florida 22nd district that was carved out in redistricting and where no incumbent was in the fray.
“Florida’s 22nd District was one of the most competitive districts for Democrats, and Pia just turned it blue,” Chintan Patel, Executive Director, Indian American Impact, said in a statement.
“Indian American Impact has been proud to support her from the beginning, and we congratulate her on her victory tonight," he said.
Ms. Dandiya is a first-generation American who has dedicated her career to strengthening communities as a high school principal, policy leader and technology innovator, according to her campaign website.
Born and raised in Palm Beach County in Florida, Ms. Dandiya started her career as a teacher and was a high school principal in Harlem.
She founded a high school with the goal of changing life trajectories for low-income students by putting them on a path to economic freedom.
Every single graduate of her high school earned admission to college, despite 86 per cent of them living in low-income households.
She was founding principal of her school at the age of 28, making her one of the youngest high school principals in the country, according to the campaign website.

GOKARNA: Three employees of a Bengaluru-based IT company died after being swept away by strong waves at Dubbansashi beach in Gokarna, Karnataka.

stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: When it comes to cheating in exams, students have never been short of inventive tricks.
From chits slipped inside shoes to formulas scribbled inside the palms of one’s hands, the methods have been as old hat as ingenious. The first-semester exams are currently under way. On Tuesday, the invigilator noticed a student wearing glasses that looked suspicious.
“The glasses were a little too big than the normal ones. Even though I felt something was amiss, I did not want to disturb the student.

After an hour and half, I walked up to him and asked if he had issues with his eyesight. I also asked him if I could take a look at his glasses,” said the invigilator.

stories.headline: Tech funding in Karnataka sees 26% increase: Report
stories.deck: Most of the capital went to late-stage companies, and late-stage funding rose by 32% to $2.7 billion
stories.bodyText:
Karnataka tech companies raised $4.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026 — a 26% increase compared to $3.7 billion raised in the first nine months of 2025 — according to the latest report by market intelligence firm Tracxn.
This marks a sharp reversal from the corresponding period in 2025, when funding in the State’s tech ecosystem had declined by 40% compared to the first nine months of 2024. This also points to a possible recovery in investor confidence.
More capital, fewer rounds
While the overall quantum of capital has gone up, the ‘Karnataka Tech: 9M 2026 Report’ has observed a drop in the number of funding rounds, which declined by 35% to 397 from 610. This translates to a higher capital concentration with a fewer number of startups.
Most of the capital went to late-stage companies. Late-stage funding rose by 32%, to $2.7 billion, suggesting greater investor confidence in mature startups that have demonstrated a viable business model, revenue growth and a sizeable customer base. This also hints at a more selective funding environment, where investors have become choosier, rather than a broad-based recovery. This is in contrast to the corresponding period in the previous year, when late-stage funding witnessed a 59% drop compared to 2024.
The largest funding rounds were led by CRED, which raised $540 million in a Series H round in June 2026, backed by Meta, followed by Sarvam’s $255 million Series B round in June 2026 and Rapido’s $240 million Series F round in May 2026. Together, these three rounds accounted for approximately $1 billion of total funding in the first nine months of 2026. Late-stage took 57% of all funding.
Seed-stage suffers
Early-stage funding also rose by 35% to $1.7 billion. However, seed-stage funding fell by 32% to $281 million, as per the report, suggesting a degree of unwillingness among investors to take risks.
According to the report, FinTech, Enterprise Applications and Auto Tech emerged as the top-funded sectors, with Bengaluru accounting for nearly all the funding raised. Mysuru ranked second with $8 million in funding, compared to $1,65,000 in the corresponding period in 2025. Other cities contributed less than 1% of the State’s total funding.

darshinis
 and petty shops across the city raising tea and coffee prices by ₹3 to ₹5 after the latest milk price revision.
Just a couple of months after tea and coffee prices were raised amid the LPG price hike and gas supply concerns, regular customers are once again feeling the pinch as their daily cuppa gets costlier. With milk now costlier by ₹8 a litre and curd by ₹14, eateries are once again passing on the increased costs to customers. A cup of coffee that earlier cost ₹20 now sells for ₹25 at some outlets, making even a routine coffee break a more expensive affair.
Milk price hike sours the cuppa
For those whose work stretches beyond regular hours, coffee and tea are often indispensable. Photographer and theatre artist Sharath K says the repeated price hikes are making even devoted coffee drinkers think twice about their daily cups.
“As we work odd hours, especially around events and gigs, coffee and tea are what keep us going. After the earlier hike this year, we had already begun sharing one cup between two people. 
Now, with a cup costing ₹25, it is getting harder for those of us who rely on several cups a day. Even a simple coffee break has become an expense we have to think twice about,” he says.
Black coffee over the regular brew?
For those living away from their families, darshinis and small eateries are go-to spots for everyday meals and beverages. Techie Chethan KM says the latest hike could nudge consumers towards cheaper alternatives.
“I usually have coffee at least twice a day. Since I live away from my family, 
darshinis are where I end up having most of my meals and beverages. But paying ₹25 for a regular cup of coffee no longer seems worth it. Switching to black coffee or black tea is probably a more convenient and economical option. It could also be a healthier alternative, depending on how much sugar and milk one consumes,” he says.
Exam season, empty pockets
Students, who rely on endless cups of tea and coffee to get through assignments, exams and project deadlines, are feeling the pinch too. Engineering student Pavan D says the hike is not limited to darshinis as even neighbourhood petty shops have revised their prices.
“During exams, assignments and project submissions, there are days when tea and coffee are almost all we survive on. We end up having several cups just to stay awake and get through the workload. Now, it is not just 
darshinis
 but even small petty shops that have raised the price of tea and coffee by ₹5. It may seem like a small amount, but when you are a student buying multiple cups every day, it adds up. It is an inconvenience,” he says.
Costlier milk leaves hotels no option
In a press statement issued on October 29, the Bengaluru Hotels Association said the steep rise in milk prices would make it difficult for hotels to absorb the extra cost without revising menu prices. “If the increase had been limited to ₹2-3 per litre, there would have been no need to increase the prices of coffee, tea or snacks in hotels,” the association said. “The steep hike will make it necessary to increase the prices of all food and beverages made using milk,” it added.
Association president PC Rao says the hike has become a burden on consumers, and hotels are being forced to pass on the additional costs. “The prices of milk-based products such as ghee, butter, paneer and cheese could also increase. We are already witnessing irregular supplies of ghee,” he says.

briefs.headline: ‘We want Kannada indie music to go global’
briefs.deck: Bengaluru duo Ashwin Mandoth and Vivek Kiran aim to take Kannada indie-rock ballad Neenillade across India and the world
briefs.bodyText:
Deepa Natarajan Lobo
Young Bengaluru musicians Ashwin Mandoth and Vivek Kiran recently released their single, 
Neenillade
. The Kannada indie-rock ballad explores feelings of emptiness and separation. What began as a dark piano idea gradually grew into a mellow track through distorted guitars, raw riffs, heavy strings and traditional drums. “As its name suggests, 
Neenillade
 is about absence — of people, and of parts of oneself,” explains Ashwin.
For the two musicians, the song’s defining moment is its opening. “The intro came out naturally during a jam session and sounded like a void, like absence itself. The rest of the song was built around this very feeling and it’s definitely a song built to stay in your head,” points out Vivek.
Neenillade
 took a year and a half to complete and is a “real labour of love,” says the duo. “The time allowed us to grow as musicians and push the song to its full potential,” notes Ashwin.
With influences ranging from KK, Charan Raj, Raghu Dixit and Bengaluru band Pineapple Express to Coldplay, Periphery and Slash, the duo hopes to create music that makes an impact both on record and on stage.
They already have music lined up for 2027 and 2028 and are even planning releases for 2029. But their larger ambition is to take Kannada indie music to bigger stages and festivals around the world while helping build a stronger live music culture at home. “We want Kannada indie music to become the biggest indie scene in India and the world, and we aim to be the pioneers of that rise — building a live culture where Kannada indie can headline big stages,” they conclude.

briefs.headline: Suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission chief planned mall, other mega projects in Yadgir: ED
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Enforcement Directorate
 (ED), probing the alleged Karnataka Public Service Commission job-for-cash scam, told a special court that suspended KPSC chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar had prepared plans for construction projects worth an estimated Rs 35-Rs 40 crore in his hometown of Shahpur in Yadgir district.
Opposing the bail petitions filed by Sahukar and fellow accused KPSC member BV Geeta, ED informed the court that it had seized architectural plans for several projects on land registered in the name of Sahukar’s wife, Vijayalakshmi. The designs reportedly included plans for malls and commercial complexes, a playground and school.
Arguments from defence counsels are scheduled to be presented before the court Wednesday.
Sahukar and Geeta were arrested by ED along two other accused, IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar and tout Basavaraj Kannale. All four are in Bengaluru Central Prison under judicial custody. During an earlier hearing on extension of judicial custody, ED had alleged that Sahukar was involved in cash transactions amounting to around Rs 10 crore with Bengaluru-based realtor SP Dayananda.
Defence counsel CH Hanumantharaya argued that Sahukar was entitled to bail under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) as he was not accused of personally receiving more than Rs 1 crore in proceeds of crime.
Opposing the plea, public prosecutor DM Maheshwari cited statements recorded by ED from a candidate and his father, who allegedly paid an advance of Rs 10 lakh to Sahukar in exchange for access to question paper and answer scripts of veterinary officer recruitment examination. According to the prosecutor, Sahukar initially demanded Rs 50 lakh, but the amount was subsequently negotiated to Rs 20 lakh as the candidate belonged to his community.
ED also raised questions over financial transactions between Sahukar and Geeta. The agency alleged that Sahukar regularly deposited Rs 75,000 into the bank account of Geeta’s daughter and also paid her educational expenses. Sahukar reportedly claimed the monthly payments were rent for a flat owned by Geeta in which he was residing. However, the prosecution pointed out that no rental agreement had been produced to substantiate the claim.
Seeking bail, Geeta’s defence counsel argued that she deserved special consideration under PMLA provisions applicable to women. But the prosecution said Geeta, a non-practising advocate who had previously served as a prosecutor with Karnataka Lokayukta, was well aware of the legal implications of her alleged actions.

briefs.headline: Video: Speeding SUV crashes into Bengaluru kebab shop after hitting parked bikes, 3 injured
briefs.deck: A Mitsubishi Pajero Sport sped through Bengaluru, crashing into parked motorcycles and the Halevooramma Kebab Centre. This reckless driving led to hot cooking oil spilling out, severely burning three individuals who were rapidly taken to a private hospital for urgent care. Miraculously, those dining nearby dodged the chaos. The vehicle has been seized by authorities, who are now investigating the…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A speeding SUV rammed into parked motorcycles before crashing into a kebab centre near Bannerghatta, on the outskirts of Bengaluru, spilling hot cooking oil on people inside and leaving three with serious burn injuries. Several others standing outside narrowly escaped. CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced on social media.
The accident took place at Hommadevanahalli, where a Mitsubishi Pajero Sport, allegedly travelling at high speed, first hit several two-wheelers parked along the roadside before crashing into Halevooramma Kebab Centre.
The three injured, identified as Basavaraj, Munikrishna and Manjesh, sustained serious burn injuries and were rushed to a private hospital, where they are undergoing treatment.
The collision damaged the shop and sent objects flying. People standing outside narrowly escaped as the SUV ploughed through the parked motorcycles and crashed into the eatery.
Bannerghatta police seized the SUV and registered a case. An investigation is underway to establish the circumstances that led to the accident.

briefs.headline: Ten years of RERA: 3,147 projects lapse in Karnataka, only 39% apply for completion
briefs.deck: The data points to a large number of projects in the State that have not reached the completion stage within their stipulated timelines
briefs.bodyText:
As the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA), 2016, completes 10 years, only 39% of the projects registered under the law have applied for completion in Karnataka, while almost 35% have lapsed, according to data compiled by the Forum for People’s Collective Efforts (FPCE), which has been at the forefront of the fight for homebuyers in Karnataka.
The State’s latest figures show that 3,147 of the 8,984 projects approved for registration with the Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) have lapsed. Only 3,580 projects have applied for completion. The data points to a large number of projects in the State that have not reached the completion stage within their stipulated timelines.
M.S. Shankar, general secretary of the FPCE, said the authorities already had details of projects whose registration periods had lapsed, adding that they should have visited these sites to ascertain their status and take preventive action.
He questioned why K-RERA could not inspect projects in advance, keep their registrations in abeyance where necessary, and freeze project bank accounts to prevent further diversion of homebuyers’ money. The organisation has also called for regular inspections of all ongoing registered projects to ensure that developers adhere to their committed timelines.
RERA-K Chairman Rakesh Singh said most of the lapsed projects were either pre-RERA projects or had been abandoned due to disputes with landowners or other reasons. He said efforts had been made to encourage developers to apply for extensions at a minimal cost, but he admitted that these efforts had not yielded the desired results.
Mr. Shankar told The Hindu that a coordination committee should be formed under the chairmanship of the Chief Secretary to ensure proper implementation of RERA in Karnataka. He proposed that the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court and the homebuyer associations be included in the committee.
Money recovery
The recovery of money awarded to homebuyers is another concern in Karnataka. As of November 1, 2026, K-RERA had issued 2,694 Recovery Revenue Certificates (RRCs), involving ₹1,253.11 crore. However, it had recovered only 356 certificates, involving ₹129.03 crore. This is only 10.29% of the total amount recovered.
Between January 23 and October 31, 2026, K-RERA issued 369 additional RRCs involving ₹171.27 crore, while recovering only ₹18.76 crore against 74 certificates.
Restructuring
These Karnataka figures form part of FPCE’s larger concerns over the implementation of RERA across the country. In a representation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the organisation has sought a fundamental restructuring of the legislation, arguing that its dual mandate of promoting the real estate sector and protecting homebuyers has compromised its consumer-protection role.
The FPCE has said that several practices that RERA was enacted to prevent continue, including diversion of funds collected from homebuyers, one-sided builder-buyer agreements, delays in possession, unauthorised changes to sanctioned plans and the handing over of homes without occupancy certificates. It has also flagged the granting of repeated project extensions without properly examining the developers’ defaults and the failure to execute refund and compensation orders obtained by homebuyers.
Based on official records from seven States, including Karnataka, the group estimates that ₹12.44 lakh crore of homebuyers’ money remains locked in delayed projects, affecting around 27.6 lakh families.
The organisation has proposed removing the promotion of the real estate sector from the mandate of RERA authorities and restructuring it as a Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act, with its administration placed under a consumer-protection ministry, such as Consumer Affairs.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru team takes the cake at ACADA 2026
briefs.deck: A team from Bengaluru represented India at the International Cake Show Australia 2026 and submitted the winning entry for cake sculpting
briefs.bodyText:
What could an artist, sculptor and baker have in common? At the recently-concluded International Cake Show Australia 2026, Anna Austin, Arati Mirji and Samie Ramachandran from Bengaluru won the World’s Best Extreme Cake Sculptors title, placing first among contestants from Australia, Japan, and Taiwan.
Team India’s winning entry was a jallikattu bull and tamer, based on the theme of Adventure and the trio had to sculpt a piece within a 12-hour time period, over two days. The cake show was hosted by the Australian Cake Artists & Decorators Association (ACADA).
While cake is a sweet something to enjoy or mark an occasion for most of us, Anna, Arati and Samie view it as their canvas. As a cake artist, Anna had interacted with Arati, a sugar flower artist, and Samie, a cake-and-sugar sculptor, so often over the past 12 years that they had forged a friendship.
Anna, founder of Cake Canvas, believed each member of Team India possessed a specific set of skills that could win them the title. While she had established a name for herself as a creator of life-size, life-like edible scultures, Arati was known for crafting sugar flowers that could fool the bees and Samie had mastered the art of sculpting cakes that could go up to 24 feet.
“Each of us had become proficient in our own set of skills and were regularly invited to teach at the same workshops and classes. Though we’ve known each other for more than a decade, this was the first time we were working on a project together,” says Samie, founder and director of Sugar Sculpt Academy.
“When the competition was announced I was sure the three of us stood a winning chance,” says Anna, adding, “The theme was chosen by reigning champions, Team Australia and our application was among the first to be selected.”
Gearing up
The team held two trial runs in India before they left for Brisbane, the contest’s venue in Australia. “We had nine months to chart out our plan of action — from what we would be creating to our individual roles in bringing it together,” says Arati, a world renown sugar flower artist, who partnered with Italian brand Saracino, to create Saracino’s Flower Paste by Arati Mirji.
Anna continues, “We had decided our roles based on our strengths — I would work on the faces and legs of both the figures and Samie would do the bodies. Arati was in charge of the fine detailing of bells, flowers and colours.”
“We had to translate a high-energy sporting movement into cake,” Arati says, adding the contest had specifications; the figurine had to be approximately 1.5 metres in height, comprising at least two-thirds edible material. “We got more points if we increased that ratio,” Arati says.
Organisers bake cake slabs as per participant requirement and provide them at the competition venue, while teams are allowed to carry the structure or frame on which they would fashion their piece. Everything else had to be crafted at the venue.
According to Samie, the team faced three, huge challenges. “We were planning to create two figures when our competitors would be perfecting just one. Second, we would be using material from brands different from those available in India, which could take some adjustment. And finally, it was winter there and the chocolate was hardening faster than we expected.”
“Moulding the chocolate to make it pliable took quite a bit of our time, and we had to tweak our plan for the second day so we didn’t fall behind,” says Anna.
Good old-fashioned, Indian jugaad also came in handy, adds Arati, who says the team used paint rollers instead of airbrushes over the figurines.
They admit the thought of working in front of a live audience was daunting, but, “once we began, the audience ceased to exist. Each of us knew what we had to do and we went ahead doing just that. There was no room for mistakes,” says Anna.
“We worked seamlessly and in sync. There was no confusion or extra chatter and we finished with 30 minutes to spare,” says Arati.
Team India utilised around 15 kilos of rice crispies and marshmallows each, 60 kilos of modelling chocolate and 20 kilos of white chocolate ganache, apart from edible colour, decorative supplies, flower paste, cocoa butter and other material.
Looking back
Samie says entering a competition was not on his bucket list, but when Anna brought up the idea, the thought of engaging “with the best as well as the reigning champions” piqued his interest. “Our submission was really good, but having been a judge of contests myself, I knew the parameters used to assess entries are different from what participants perceive.”
The team recalled the challenges they faced — from landing sponsors to transporting the structure across the sea and working with new material — all of which paled in comparison with their win.
Arati says her journey as a baker, let alone a sugar flower artist, was quite accidental. “At a friend’s home, we were served cake she had just pulled out of the oven. The entire experience was simple and yet so enjoyable — that we could share something so wholesome that was prepared at home made me want to bake too.”
She enrolled at a culinary academy to learn and at the time, sugar flowers were not yet making waves. “Most of the tools were not available in India at the time, but after attending a basic course I was hooked,” she says, adding she went online and taught herself.
“Suger flowers have to be assembled one petal at a time and need to be kept dry at all times; humidity or moisture ruin them. Generally, a single showpiece has 12 varieties of flowers and takes about a month and half to create if you work six hours a day,” she says, which makes their feat at ACADA all the more remarkable.
For Samie, transporting the main frame was a challenge. “Though it was a plus for the team to be able to carry the structure, the fact that we were baking the rest from scratch was intense. That we were crafting two figures meant our time was essentially halved which only added to our task.”
“I felt the Australian entry with an underwater theme was really good, but I suppose we had the edge with more complex characters,” he says.
For Anna, with an MfA degree from Kochi, cakes were “a change of medium to an edible format”. She started creating realistic figurines in 2012 and by 2014, was gaining recognition for her craft with international awards.
Now, she says, the challenge is to defend their title. ACADA has announced that Team India has automatically qualified for the 2027 International Cake-Off Championships to be be held in July and August next year.

NEW DELHI: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories even keeping its fiscal consolidation road map largely unaffected, as the resulting revenue loss is likely to be limited to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY28, a report said on Tuesday.

stories.headline: 4-layer motor cover for new private cars, 2-wheelers from Dec. 15: IRDAI
stories.deck: Regulator’s directive follows Supreme Court order mandating a policy structure covering third-party liability, legal liability to occupants, personal accident and own damage
stories.bodyText:
Insurance regulator IRDAI has set a December 15 deadline for all general insurers to offer new private cars and two-wheelers a four-layer motor insurance policy covering third party liability, legal liability to occupants, personal accident and own damage of the vehicle.
The cover will comprise both mandatory and optional components, with the optional covers available on payment of an additional premium.
Third party insurance, as is currently the case, and the personal accident cover for the owner will be mandatory.
The optional components will be coverage for legal liability towards occupants or pillion riders, including employees of the insured; personal accident cover for occupants or pillion riders, including any driver other than the owner-driver; and the own damage cover.
In a circular to general insurers, which follows the Supreme Court directions in a case, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India said the four-layer motor cover structure, uniform wordings along with the option form will come into force from December 15. Getting the option form completed by the customer is mandatory for all insurance policies issued to this category of vehicles.
Specify premium charged
Apart from following uniform wordings, the schedule issued by the insurer should reflect the actual coverage offered along with premium charged against each section in a transparent manner, the regulator said in the circular on implementation of the Supreme Court directions.
The Supreme Court passed the directions to bring clarity on availability of various policy options to the vehicle-owner and to make an informed choice of purchasing suitable insurance protection. It said IRDAI in consultation with General Insurance Council and insurance companies should formulate uniform policy wordings for the optional covers.
IRDAI said it is mandatory for insurers to issue Customer Information Sheet at the point of sale. On the optional components, the customers can opt in by tick whether offline or online. The insurers can continue to innovate the coverage and determine the pricing of the own damage covers, in consonance with market forces, it said.
For existing policies too, the optional covers can be made available on payment of an additional premium.

Adani Airport Holdings CEO Arun Bansal on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) said international airlines unwilling to shift their operations to the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) could stop flying to Mumbai.
The disagreement comes as Adani-owned Mumbai International Airport Ltd. (MIAL) prepares to undertake redevelopment work at Terminal 1, necessitating the relocation of a portion of flight operations currently handled at Terminal 2 to Navi Mumbai. Defending the airport operator’s position, Mr. Bansal said airlines had been given notice to vacate the existing facilities from April, adding that where they chose to operate subsequently was their decision.

briefs.headline: TaMo looks at manufacturing Iveco in India

MUMBAI: 
N Chandrasekaran
, who became chair of Iveco following 
Tata Motors
' biggest acquisition, said the combined ₹21 billion commercial vehicle group expects volumes, revenues and margins to grow over the next five years, as both companies explore opportunities to expand in each other's markets, including manufacturing Iveco products in India.
Speaking in Turin, Chandrasekaran said the combination brings together complementary product portfolios and geographic footprints, uniting two profitable and cash-generative businesses with operations spanning India, Europe and Latin America.
The acquisition, Tata Motors' biggest since its purchase of Jaguar Land Rover in 2008, has created the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle manufacturer in the trucks-above-six-tonnes segment, with annual sales of nearly six lakh vehicles.

The combined group operates in more than 130 countries, with 27 manufacturing plants, 25 research and development centres and over 73,000 employees.
Tata Motors completed the initial settlement of its tender offer last week, securing nearly 90% stake in Iveco for about ₹4 billion and making the Italian truckmaker an indirect subsidiary. Despite the combination, Iveco will continue to operate from its headquarters in Turin, he said.
At the press conference, Tata Motors MD Girish Wagh, who has joined the Iveco board as a non-executive director, recalled the Indian company's long-standing association with the Italian city. briefs.headline: SBI net rises 14% to 23k crore, shares slip 1.8%
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and lower loan loss provisions. Net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago, while loan loss provisions fell 33% to Rs 2,759 crore as asset quality improved.
However, the bank's shares fell 1.8% to Rs 969 as investors were disappointed with the 7.3% growth in operating profit to Rs 34,226 crore. The increase was held back by a 24% decline in other income to Rs 11,777 crore.
Addressing newspersons, SBI chairman CS Setty reiterated the bank's guidance of 10-11% deposit growth and 14-15% credit growth. The bank has a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore, he said.
"If nominal GDP growth is around 12 to 12.5%, normally the SBI credit growth rate is 3 to 4% over that and that is where the guidance of 14 to 15% is coming from," explained Setty.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
The bank does not face any immediate compulsion to raise deposit rates, given its comfortable liquidity position. SBI had excess statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) holdings of more than Rs 4 lakh crore as of Sept 30, providing adequate headroom to fund credit growth, he said.

briefs.headline: Won't open up dairy sector or let in genetically modified products: Piyush Goyal
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister 
Piyush Goyal
 Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector in any free trade agreement and will not allow imports of genetically modified products, describing both as "very sensitive" issues for the country.
Addressing students of Kirori Mal College, Goyal said India has "never ever" compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts.
"We are sensitive to opening up to certain agricultural produce, certain goods that we are very strong on like marine products. We are very sensitive to opening our dairy. In fact, till date, we have never opened up dairy for anybody. 
US Midterm Election Results 2026
We are very sensitive not to allow any genetically modified products to come to India and we have never allowed it and we'll never allow it in the future," he said.
He said, "We are sensitive to our religious sensitivities. So very often in foreign countries, they use calf meat or Rennet while producing their dairy products. We don't allow that in India. It is strictly got to be certified... so that religious sensitivities of the large parts of India are not hurt."
Rennet is an enzyme used in cheese-making, traditionally obtained from the stomach lining of young calves. PTI

briefs.headline: Industry bodies debate LTCG pitch ahead of pre-budget discussions
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of the pre-budget consultation with revenue secretary Arvind Shrivastava on Wednesday, industry bodies were working out their final wish list on long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) - the most-discussed budgetary proposal this year.
Executives at industry associations said that there were competing views from members and tax experts and a final call on how the demand should be worded was yet to be taken. While the proposal is not completely new, it has got a major thrust amid stagnant stock market indices and negative returns for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) due to a weak rupee. The call gained further momentum after the Centre scrapped the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on FPI investment in govt securities in June as part of a strategy to support the rupee.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
On Tuesday, while some of the bodies were finetuning their position, most strident were FPIs, demanding that govt abolish the tax at least for them. There are some supporters of this among industry representatives as well. But politically, especially with mutual funds and retail investors emerging as a large investor community, it may not be possible for govt to only focus on overseas investors and ignore the claims of domestic investors -- more so, when complaints about high GST and personal income tax rates have just subsided.
With revenue impact being a concern, there is some discussion around a graded reduction in LTCG. So, some industry representatives have suggested that short-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax (STT) be retained in their current form and LTCG in year 1 also be left unchanged at 12.5%. But those who hold the shares longer should be charged concessional LTCG, which could fall to zero over three-five years.
There is also a school of thought that STT should be abolished and LTCG be retained. Then, there are suggestions that STT should apply to F&O but be removed for the cash segment.
There is also a section which believes that FPIs will come once stock market valuations correct further and the rupee stabilises.
As finance minister has said in her public statements, she is keeping track of the debate. The outcome will be known only on Feb 1 when she presents a record-equalling tenth budget.

briefs.headline: Cyber risks: Banks working on coordinated response
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The banking industry is working on a coordinated response to rising cybersecurity risks, with banks looking to establish a structured mechanism for sharing information on cyber incidents and an industry-level sandbox to test frontier artificial intelligence (AI) models in a regulated environment.
State Bank of India chairman CS Setty said Indian Banks' Association (IBA) was working on both initiatives to help lenders identify vulnerabilities and respond faster to emerging threats.
"As more and more digitalisation happens, the digital surface area is increasing. What we call attack surface area is increasing. And the security and digital adoption need not be mutually exclusive," said Setty. He said govt, public sector institutions and private entities were collectively working to ensure that cyber incidents did not undermine trust in digital systems.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
IBA had also developed a comprehensive framework to address AI-related cybersecurity concerns. However, Setty said, a key priority was to strengthen information sharing across banks and financial institutions.
While incidents were already being reported to regulators and security agencies, a structured mechanism to alert other banks as soon as an incident occurred would enable them to take preventive measures immediately. "This is something that we are seriously working under the IBA," he said.
The other initiative involves creating an industry-level sandbox where frontier AI models can be tested in a regulated and controlled environment.

briefs.headline: AI weighs ordering more wide body aircraft: Air India CEO
briefs.bodyText:
To focus on boosting revenue, reducing cost & regain market share: Gebremariam
NEW DELHI: Having "punched below its weight" for too long, 
Air India
 is now considering a fresh order for more wide body aircraft to "regain market share from competition " as that "business belongs to AI".
While the "short-term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the deep in red airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency, said AI CEO Tewolde Gebremariam, while outlining his plans for the carrier for the first time.
"Air India is Tata's baby and they want to see it grow. It is an opportunity for AI to be (back with) Tatas. Yes, there are challenges and profitability is a concern, but together we will make AI great again by keeping one eye on navigating headwinds today and the other on the future," the veteran from Ethiopian Airlines said at Aviation India 2026 on Tuesday.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
AI lost a record Rs 22,238 crore last fiscal and the group (including AI Express) has bled over Rs 58,000 crore since the Tata takeover in Jan 2022, something that is causing concern among promoters Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, with the Maharaja seeking fresh fund infusion. While the report of tragic AI 171 Ahmedabad crash last June is awaited, continuing geopolitical issues pose a greater challenge to Indian carriers due to the closure of Pakistan airspace for them.
Tewolde said how AI is tackling these issues. "We have created multi function cost teams and the focus is on increasing efficiency. We are increasing synergy between AI and AI Express so that they can share common functions (and cut costs). We have to bring our unit cost lower to the industry level," he said.
For increasing revenue, AI is "rebalancing" its hub network as no one knows how long the Pakistan airspace closure will last. "Pakistan airspace closure affects flights between the West and Delhi. So, we are adding more flights to the West from Mumbai and to South and Southeast from Delhi. We are exploring Bengaluru as our third hub," he said.
AI Group has about 600 aircraft on order from Airbus and Boeing, with only 80 of them being wide body. With an eye on increasing traffic to and from India, and the 3 crore Indian diaspora globally "wanting to travel AI" once the airline improves overall, Tewolde feels there is a case for "increasing wide body order" without disclosing any numbers.
"We have many of them (wide bodies), but we need more. The market demand is huge and the network is not served enough. India can establish global hubs in Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru. We have to regain market share from (foreign) competition with the right product. Air India was punching below its weight. It may take some time but that will change."

briefs.headline: Pre-Diwali fireworks: Sensex up over 2.4k points in two days
briefs.bodyText:

sensex

Combined with a 1,233-point gain on Monday, the index is now up 2,458 points or 3.3%, the index's best two-day gaining streak since April 8 this year. The gains came on the back of nearly Rs 10,000-crore net buying by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in the secondary market in two sessions.
On Tuesday, sensex opened the session up about 600 points, touched an intraday high of 77,093 points (up 1,400 points) and closed just a tad off that level at 76,918 points. On NSE, Nifty too followed a similar trajectory and closed at 23,811 points, up 370 points or 1.6%. Ahead of

briefs.headline: Government eyes 15k crore from PSU land monetisation
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Centre is on course to monetise land worth Rs 15,000 crore belonging to central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) during the current financial year through National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC), with transactions amounting to Rs 9,000 crore already finalised so far this year, an official told TOI.
The land monetisation pipeline for this year includes properties of troubled telecom twins 
BSNL
 and MTNL, apart from Rashtriya Ispat Nigam (RINL), defunct Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT), ITL and Hindustan Insecticides (HIL), among others.
The NLMC is also targeting additional monetisation of MTNL properties worth Rs 5,000-6,000 crore over the next two years. The telecom PSU, with operations in Delhi and Mumbai, has prime land, including apartments and office complexes. 
US Midterm Election Results 2026
It had identified properties for disposal several years ago but progress has been slow. The telecom company, which has been taken over by BSNL, carries a substantial debt burden, with outstandings of around Rs 10,000 crore, according to the official. BSNL also is not out of the woods either, despite govt pumping in thousands of crores for "strategic reasons".
The official said that while transactions of Rs 9,000 crore have been finalised, money is yet to flow in, with more properties targeted to be put up for sale in the remaining months of 2026-27.
On Tuesday, NLMC organised a pre-bid meeting for the e-auction of a land parcel owned by HIL in Delhi at a reserve price of Rs 829 crore.
"A number of CPSEs reached out to NLMC, after it successfully e-auctioned 180 plots of RINL in Visakhapatnam in two phases, with the first phase netting Rs 366 crore against a reserve price of Rs 312 crore," NLMC CEO Rohan Thakur told reporters at the event. HIL chairperson and MD Kuldeep Singh told TOI that the next move will see sale of a residential land parcel in the city, which is in vicinity of one currently under auction.
Set up in 2022 as part of govt's broader effort to put underutilised public assets to productive use, NLMC functions under the finance ministry and is mandated to monetise non-core land assets of CPSEs and govt agencies. The money collected from such sales provides an avenue for debt-laden companies to reduce debt and strengthen their balance sheets.

stories.headline: 'Learned some great lessons': McCullum reflects on Pak setback ahead of Aus challenge
stories.deck: Brendon McCullum emphasizes the critical role of the upcoming series against Australia in gearing up for the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. Following England's disappointing performance in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, with just one victory, the coach aims to evaluate player development and fitness. The squad includes several newcomers who will benefit from this one-day experience.
stories.bodyText:
England head coach 
Brendon McCullum
 is hoping his team can turn the disappointment of their recent ODI tri-series campaign in Pakistan into valuable lessons as they prepare for a challenging white-ball tour of Australia.
England arrived in Perth on Monday for an eight-match assignment against Australia, featuring three ODIs and five T20Is. The series gets underway on November 13 and will serve as an important part of their preparations for next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, according to the ICC website.
The tour also marks England's return to Australia following their disappointing Ashes campaign earlier this year. However, McCullum is keen to look forward rather than dwell on the past, viewing the upcoming contests as an opportunity to assess his team's progress and methods.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
"Firstly, it's nice to be back. An Australia tour is always a great tour. The cricket's always pretty competitive. We'll play at some great stadiums, against a good side, and continue to test our methods, towards the one-day World Cup," McCullum said.
The England coach also stressed the importance of maintaining an aggressive approach while using the demanding schedule to improve the players' fitness.
"We know we need to keep getting better, but we've been presented with some good opportunities, and this will be one of those in the next couple of weeks. 
We want to play a high-octane, robust style of play, which demands fitness elements to it. So for us, this is a great opportunity to have a little fitness block in and around the demand of this series," he added.
McCullum keen to build on Pakistan tri-series experience
England had a mixed outing in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, where they managed only one win across four matches and failed to secure a place in the final.
There were, however, encouraging individual performances. Captain 
Harry Brook
 and opener 
Ben Duckett
 impressed with the bat, while Liam Dawson, Sonny Baker and Jamie Overton contributed with the ball.
Despite falling short of their target, McCullum believes the tournament offered important exposure, particularly for a relatively inexperienced squad that needs more time in one-day cricket.
Reflecting on the campaign, he admitted that the result was disappointing but highlighted the benefits of facing different opponents, adapting to varying conditions and dealing with different tactical challenges.
"It was disappointing. Obviously, it was great to play in the tri-series. With the view towards the World Cup, the ability to be able to bounce between games, and different tactics, and different oppositions was good," McCullum said.
"We obviously didn't quite achieve what we wanted to, but we played some really good cricket and learned some great lessons. They should hold you in good stead in 12 months. We've got a pretty inexperienced team. These guys haven't played a lot of one-day cricket, so any opportunity to get experience and education, and those pressure moments, so that you can start to just understand a little bit better, it's going to be good," he added.
The 2027 World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, giving England a year to strengthen their preparations and build a settled combination.
