stories.headline: Four decades after his death, how Jalandhar keeps the spirit of Surjit alive
stories.deck: More than four decades after his death in a road accident in 1984, Surjit - a World Cup winner, an Olympian and an Arjuna Award recipient - remains woven into the sporting fabric of the region.
stories.bodyText:
JALANDHAR: Every city has its legends. In hockey-loving Jalandhar, Surjit Singh Randhawa is more than a legend. He remains a presence. His name greets visitors at the stadium named after him and lives on in an academy that continues to produce international players, six of whom are currently part of the Indian team, including captain 
Harmanpreet Singh
.
More than four decades after his death in a road accident in 1984, Surjit - a World Cup winner, an Olympian and an Arjuna Award recipient - remains woven into the sporting fabric of the region. The ongoing Asian Champions Trophy here has brought the spotlight back on the man widely regarded as one of India's greatest full-backs and penalty-corner specialist. It was Surjit's equaliser against Pakistan in the 1975 World Cup final that paved the way for Ashok Kumar's title-winning goal.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
But for those who knew him, Surjit was not merely a hockey star. He was a teammate, a mentor, a friend and, perhaps most importantly, a symbol of what Punjab hockey once was and still aspires to be.
Former India captain Ajit Pal Singh, who was India's captain in 1975, remembers Surjit as one of the pillars of that golden generation. "He was a dependable defender, a penalty-corner specialist and a fighter to the core. As captain, I always had complete faith in him as a teammate," said Ajit Pal.
Brigadier Harcharan Singh, another Olympian and three-time World Cup medallist, first saw Surjit as a teenager at a village tournament in 1969. Recognising his talent, he helped the youngster gain admission to Sports College, Jalandhar. Within a few years, the boy established himself as one of the world's finest defenders. What separated Surjit from others, according to those who played with him, was his relentless work ethic.
That dedication transformed him into a player opponents feared and goalkeepers dreaded. Former India goalkeeper Alloysius Edwards never had the chance to play against Surjit but grew up hearing stories about the Punjab legend's ferocious hitting power. "I once heard from a goalkeeper playing for JCT that he fractured a finger while attempting to stop one of Surjit's penalty-corner strikes," said Edwards, who represented India at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics and currently coaches Punjab & Sind Bank's hockey team in Jalandhar.
 His reputation as a penalty-corner expert became so great that many in Punjab draw a direct line from Prithipal Singh to Surjit Singh and then to present-day India captain Harmanpreet Singh, another defender who is equally lethal from penalty corners.

stories.headline: Bracewell expects even contests in one-dayers
stories.deck: When asked about how spinners need to evolve to succeed in ODI cricket where the deck is loaded against them, he highlighted the importance of being unpredictable
stories.bodyText:
New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell felt that the rule change introduced last year, which lets teams choose one ball for the last 16 overs of the game, has also helped spinners in ODIs.
While two new balls are used from each end from the start to the 34th over, after that, one ball will be used for the rest of the match. This was done primarily to help bowlers get some reverse swing with a slightly older ball.
“I think the ball gets a little bit softer. So perhaps spinners are bowling more in the last 10 overs. And I guess when that ball does get soft, it becomes a little bit harder to hit out to the boundary. So it can be a positive for a spin bowler to be bowling at the back end,” said Bracewell.
When asked about how spinners need to evolve to succeed in ODI cricket where the deck is loaded against them, he highlighted the importance of being unpredictable.
“There’s not much that you can change in terms of your line and length. So you’ve got to try and get the ball to behave slightly differently off the surface through variation in pace or the way that you hold the ball to get it to just react slightly differently off the surface,” he added.
Looking ahead to the ODI series, the 35-year-old expected a tight contest. “It’s two evenly matched teams. We had a great series in India at the start of the year, winning it 2-1, and I think India will will want to right some wrongs”.

briefs.headline: PV Sindhu concerned over financial woes on Europe tour

briefs.bodyText:
HYDERABAD: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has expressed concern over the financial difficulties faced by Indian shuttlers during their four-tournament European campaign, warning that the lack of institutional support could jeopardise the careers of promising youngsters.
India’s European swing covered tournaments in Finland, Denmark, France and Germany. With Sports Authority of India (SAI) assistance falling through, several players had to meet expenses out of pocket or seek help from organisations such as Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ). Some younger shuttlers competed without coaches, while others withdrew from tournaments.
Reacting on X, Sindhu highlighted the huge disparity between badminton and tennis earnings, pointing out that players in both sports face comparable expenses but vastly different prize money.

“A first-round exit at Wimbledon earns £80,000. Winning the China Open, one of badminton’s richest tournaments, earns $140,000. Lose in the first round? Just $2,000,” she wrote on X.
Travel, coaching, physiotherapy and other support costs remain substantial in both sports, she said, adding that she had discussed the disparity with former Indian tennis star Rohan Bopanna.
Sindhu stressed that not everyone has access to sponsorships and private support. “I’ve been fortunate to have wonderful sponsors, but not everyone has that privilege,” she said. “If I can find ways to fund my tour. But what about the 18-year-old chasing her dreams?” she asked.

briefs.headline: Man United stage stunning comeback against Roma, PSG smash records in 6-0 rout
briefs.deck: In a thrilling Champions League showdown, Manchester United staged a remarkable comeback, rallying from a two-goal deficit to triumph 3-2 against Roma. Simultaneously, Paris Saint-Germain made headlines with a stunning 6-0 victory over Villarreal, scoring four times in just 17 minutes. Barcelona handed Aston Villa a resounding 3-0 defeat, marking their first loss in the tournament, while Bayern…
briefs.bodyText:
Manchester United
 produced a remarkable turnaround to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday, recovering from a disastrous start at Old Trafford to secure a much-needed victory for under-pressure coach Michael Carrick.
While United stole the spotlight with their comeback, Paris Saint-Germain delivered an equally emphatic performance, thrashing Villarreal 6-0 after scoring four times inside the opening 17 minutes. The French champions also set a new Champions League record for the fastest team to reach four goals in a match.
Elsewhere, Barcelona ended Aston Villa's unbeaten run in the competition with a 3-0 victory, while Bayern Munich registered a 2-0 away win against Atletico Madrid.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
Man United turn the tables on Roma after nightmare start
United's evening at Old Trafford appeared headed for another setback after Roma raced into a two-goal lead within the opening 17 minutes. It was the fastest the English side had conceded twice in a European fixture at their home ground.
Matias Soule opened the scoring in the 11th minute before Donyell Malen converted a penalty to leave the hosts facing an uphill battle. Roma had further opportunities to extend their advantage before the interval.
The contest, however, took a dramatic turn after the restart. Bruno Fernandes converted a penalty at the second attempt to bring United back into the game before Matheus Cunha struck twice, finding the net in the 83rd and 86th minutes. Cunha was subsequently sent off.
The victory provided some relief for Carrick, who was careful not to get carried away by the result.
"I'm not getting too carried away with things," Carrick said. "I think it's an important night. I think it's important for some of the players to have the feeling that they maybe haven't had here before."
Protests give way to celebrations at Old Trafford
The comeback celebrations were a far cry from the tense atmosphere earlier in the evening, when a section of United supporters attempted to interrupt the match by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch.
The protest was aimed at the club's American owners, the Glazer family, with fans continuing their long-standing demand for them to sell their controlling stake in the club.
A small number of tennis balls were thrown in the 21st minute, marking 21 years since the Glazers completed their leveraged buyout of Manchester United.
Fernandes said the team believed it could turn the game around after the break, with the home crowd continuing to back them.
"We knew after halftime that we still had the fans with us and we felt that at any moment we could change that with a goal, with something. Fortunately for us, we did it today," he told Amazon Prime.
"Hopefully this win today gives the start of something good for us."
For Roma, the defeat brought back unpleasant memories of their recent collapse against Real Madrid, when they conceded three goals in the final 10 minutes of a 4-3 loss last month.
PSG smash Champions League record in 6-0 demolition
PSG underlined their credentials as serious contenders for another European crown with a commanding 6-0 victory over Villarreal.
Luis Enrique's side, chasing a third consecutive Champions League title, were ruthless despite missing injured forwards Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.
The visitors effectively settled the contest within the first 17 minutes at El Madrigal. Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all found the net in a stunning opening spell.
According to UEFA, no team had previously scored four goals so quickly in a Champions League match.
Ruiz added another goal in the second half before 17-year-old David Boly marked his competition debut by scoring four minutes after coming on as a substitute.
PSG became the only team to reach 12 points in the competition.
Ruiz acknowledged the difficulty of recovering after such a damaging start for Villarreal.
"Conceding four goals so quickly is difficult for any team," he said. "You prepare for a match, and then to have four goals scored against you, it's a real blow. We don't look at the scoreboard, we always try to stick to our own style of play and our own rhythm."
Bayern Munich overcome Atletico Madrid
Bayern Munich secured a 2-0 victory away at Atletico Madrid, although newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane failed to get on the scoresheet.
The German side broke the deadlock in the 54th minute when Lennart Karl capitalised on a defensive mistake. Konrad Laimer then doubled the advantage 20 minutes later, finishing into the roof of the net after receiving a precise delivery from Kane.
The result took Bayern to eight points from four matches in the league phase.
Barcelona end Aston Villa's perfect run
Barcelona handed Aston Villa their first defeat of the Champions League campaign with a convincing 3-0 win at Camp Nou.
Lamine Yamal gave the hosts an early advantage with a seventh-minute strike before Raphinha took control after the break, scoring twice to complete the victory.
The result lifted Barcelona to second place in the standings, ahead of third-placed Villa on goal difference. Their only defeat in the competition so far has come against PSG.
Sporting, Galatasaray among other winners
Sporting Lisbon secured a 1-0 victory over Shakhtar Donetsk despite having announced their decision to part ways with coach Rui Borges a day earlier.
Under reserve coach Tiago Fernandes, the Portuguese side claimed their third Champions League win of the season. Issa Doumbia scored the decisive goal at Stamford Bridge.
Galatasaray also picked up three points, beating Stuttgart 2-0 at RAMS Park. Aleksey Batrakov settled the contest with two goals in the space of three minutes, scoring in the 12th and 15th minutes.
Inter Milan defeated Feyenoord 3-0, while LASK registered a 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava. Bodø/Glimt and Lille, meanwhile, played out a goalless draw.

briefs.headline: ‘I'll be the fielding coach’: Ex-cricketer mocks India as BCCI invites applications
briefs.deck: Michael Vaughan has spotlighted India's ongoing struggles with fielding as the BCCI seeks a new fielding coach. Recent matches, particularly during the Women's T20 World Cup, have revealed troubling catching mistakes, including in a series against Zimbabwe. With the BCCI insisting on high standards for applicants, India's tour of South Africa will be crucial for enhancing their performance and…
briefs.bodyText:
Former England captain 
Michael Vaughan
 took a cheeky dig at India's catching woes after the 
BCCI
 invited applications for the position of fielding coach for the Senior Women's National Team.
Reacting to the announcement on X, Vaughan wrote: "I will be the fielding coach."
Vaughan's post
The BCCI has set November 16 as the deadline for applications for the fielding coach's position, along with that of head physiotherapist for the Senior Men's National Team.
Vaughan's remark comes at a time when India's fielding standards have been under scrutiny following a series of costly lapses. The team's catching problems were particularly evident during the Women's T20 World Cup 2026, where India dropped 10 catches across five group-stage matches.
US Midterm Election Results 2026
Three of those dropped chances came against South Africa, with Marizanne Kapp making India pay after receiving multiple lifelines. India eventually suffered a group-stage exit, with their fielding attracting widespread criticism.
Head coach 
Amol Muzumdar
 had acknowledged the shortcomings, admitting that the team needed to improve across all three departments, including batting, bowling and fielding.
However, the problem has continued beyond the global tournament. 
India dropped four catches during their three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe before missing another four opportunities in the opening ODI of the subsequent series.
Wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh was among those to struggle, dropping two catches, including a regulation opportunity behind the stumps. 
Deepti Sharma and Kranti Gaud also missed chances, while India failed to convert a couple of run-out opportunities.
Although India completed a 3-0 sweep in the ODI series, the repeated fielding errors have raised questions about the team's efforts to address the issue.
The BCCI has laid down specific eligibility criteria for the fielding coach's role. Applicants must have either represented India or another country at the international level, hold a minimum BCCI Level 'B' coaching certification or an equivalent qualification along with at least 30 first-class matches, or have coached an international team for one season or a T20 franchise or state team for at least two seasons.
India's next assignment will be an all-format tour of South Africa in December. The teams will play a one-off Test in Gqeberha from December 9, followed by three ODIs from December 16 and three T20Is from December 26.

Seifert still goes for the pull but gets a big top edge as the ball climbs on him. It spoons towards mid on, where substitute fielder Ruturaj Gaikwad takes a simple catch. New Zealand slip to 73 for 3, with Seifert falling after a decent start.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, Short on the body with good bounce, Seifert swivels and pulls in front of square on the leg side. The man from deep square leg runs to his left and tidies it up. Two runs taken.
DRINKS! Despite losing a couple of wickets inside 10 overs, New Zealand have recovered well here. Tim Seifert is going at a good rate, and every run he scores will hurt Naman Dhir, who dropped him early in the game. Daryl Mitchell has also started positively, as these two will look to make this a significant partnership. India have bowled well, but in the field, they have missed a couple of run-out chances, but overall the pacers have been good so far.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, FOUR! Some shot, that! Short of a length, around off, angling in. Daryl Mitchell opens up his stance by clearing his front leg away and swats it over the mid on fielder for a cracking boundary.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, On a length, on fourth stump. Mitchell hangs back and stabs it to the cover fielder.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Good length, on off, Mitchell rocks back and punches it back to Anshul.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, At 138 kph, bashed hard into the deck, on off. It holds on a touch and Seifert waits back before pulling it over mid-wicket for a single.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, Short of a length, outside off, Tim rides the bounce and fends it to short cover.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, Length on middle and leg, Seifert blocks off the back foot.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, Good effort in the deep! Back of a length, outside off, Seifert punches it crisply off the back foot through cover-point. Naman Dhir covers a lot of ground to his right and slides to make the stop. The replay shows that it is a clean save. Three runs taken.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, SIX! Fantastic shot! Lands it full on off, Seifert hits it through the line, lofting it cleanly over the long off fence for a six. He holds his pose, savouring the moment.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, Hits the length hard, on top of middle, Seifert rocks back and bunts it back to the bowler.
Gurnoor Brar to Daryl Mitchell, A bit back of a length, on off, Daryl waits on it and taps it in front of mid on for another quick run.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, Angled on the pads, Seifert knocks the full ball down to mid on for a quick single.
Gurnoor Brar to Tim Seifert, On the money! Shapes the ball in from off, full in length, Seifert is pinned in the crease, thrusts his bat in front and keeps it out to the off side.
Gurnoor Brar joins the attack. A little delay with Tim Seifert needing some attention, but he is good to go now.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Fuller than a length, on off, Mitchell presses forward and blocks it right under his eyes.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Length ball, outside off, Mitchell knocks it to short cover.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Beaten! Top-drawer bowling, this. Hits the deck hard, just outside off. Mitchell gets squared up as he looks to punch it away, but the ball kicks up, nips away and zips past the outside edge.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, At 137 kph, full on fourth stump, Mitchell strides forward and defends it solidly back to the bowler.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, A bit too full, outside off, Seifert drives it to the right of mid off and sets off for a single. The fielder gets across, picks the ball and nails the direct hit at the batting end, but Mitchell is safely in.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Nips in a touch, around off and full. Mitchell, as he usually does, walks a couple of steps down and tries to defend, but gets an inside edge. The ball rolls through mid-wicket for a single.
Auqib Nabi to Daryl Mitchell, A length-delivery angled into the batter, Mitchell hangs back and knocks it through mid on for a single.
Auqib Nabi to Daryl Mitchell, Full and on the fourth stump, Daryl gets forward and pushes it to mid off.
Auqib Nabi to Daryl Mitchell, Better! Attacks the stumps with a length ball, Mitchell stabs it to the right of the bowler.
Auqib Nabi to Daryl Mitchell, SIX! Gets the distance! The keeper is up to the stumps, but that doesn't matter as it is a juicy half-volley, on off, Mitchell doesn't spare it as he tonks it over long off for a six. The 50 comes up for New Zealand!
Auqib Nabi to Daryl Mitchell, Nagging length, kicks up a bit on top of off, Mitchell gets a stride forward, then hangs back and dabs it towards Axar at backward point.
Auqib Nabi to Tim Seifert, Fuller and around off, Seifert drives it to the left of mid off for a single.
Quite an eventful Powerplay. A couple of wickets, a dropped catch, and a couple of run out chances as well. It's Powerplay 2 time and India will be allowed to have a maximum of 4 fielders outside the ring till the 40th over. Auqib Nabi (3-0-19-0) comes back with a change of ends, replacing Arshdeep Singh.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Hits the deck hard, on off, Daryl Mitchell is solid in is defense again.
Shreyas Iyer is the stand-in captain for India as Gill is off the field for the moment.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Short of a length and on off, Daryl Mitchell dabs it down in front of point.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, On a length and on middle, Daryl Mitchell steps across and keeps it out to the leg side.
Anshul Kamboj to Daryl Mitchell, Full again and on off, Daryl Mitchell gets half-forward and blocks it out.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, Fuller and on middle, Tim Seifert tucks it to the right of mid-wicket for a single.
Anshul Kamboj to Tim Seifert, Hard length and on middle, nips back in a bit, Tim Seifert stays back to play at it but misses and gets hit on his gloves.
Arshdeep Singh to Daryl Mitchell, Comes 'around the wicket, serves this full and outside off, Daryl Mitchell leaves it alone.
Arshdeep Singh to Daryl Mitchell, FOUR! Put away! Dug into the surface, on middle. Daryl Mitchell picks up the length early, gets on top of it and heaves it away to the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary to get off the mark.
Arshdeep Singh to Daryl Mitchell, Beaten! Back of a length and around off, angling away. Daryl Mitchell looks to punch it away but gets beaten on the outside edge.
So two massive wickets for the tourists in the Powerplay, both through Arshdeep. Daryl Mitchell, in at number 4, is the next batter.
Arshdeep Singh to Henry Nicholls, OUT! TAKEN! Arshdeep Singh has the last laugh here. He bangs this into the pitch, on middle, and gets some extra bounce off the deck. Henry Nicholls stands back and tries to pull it with his front leg up in the air, but he fails to transfer his weight fully. The ball hits him high on the bat and flies straight to mid-wicket, where Naman Dhir makes no mistake this time. Arshdeep is fired up here. New Zealand are 40/2 now.
Arshdeep Singh to Henry Nicholls, FOUR! Not from the middle of the bat, but gets the result! A cross-seam delivery, full and on middle. Henry Nicholls comes down the track to hoick it across the line but gets it from the inside half of the bat. It goes between mid on and mid-wicket and races to the fence for a boundary.

briefs.headline: Tenerife striker’s death after on-field collision a painful reminder for Indian fans
briefs.bodyText:
Panaji: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday.
The 30-year-old, who was chasing a pass on the break into the rival half, collided heavily with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his penalty area, and suffered head and chest injuries. The striker received treatment on the pitch for about 15 minutes before being taken to hospital.
The goalkeeper was sent off, and the match was abandoned due to the seriousness of the injury.
Tenerife initially said De Miguel’s “situation is stable but remains serious.” His condition worsened and he was pronounced dead early Tuesday morning.
“Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, we at CD Tenerife announce the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” the club said in a statement on Tuesday. 
US Midterm Election Results 2026
“There are no words of comfort. There is absolutely nothing that can ease this overwhelming sense of sadness.”
When the incident occurred, Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time. De Miguel chased a long ball that was lobbed into the opposite half but clashed with Owono, who had raced towards the halfway mark. The goalkeeper’s knee appeared to collide with the striker after which he fell, and lay motionless on the pitch.
The incident will be a painful reminder for Indian football fans of a similar on-field clash, and death, when Dempo SC striker Cristiano Junior collided with Mohun Bagan goalkeeper Subrata Paul in the final of the Federation Cup in 2004. The match continued for the remaining 12 minutes while the Brazilian was taken to the hospital, where he was declared brought dead.
Hailing from Madrid, De Miguel started his career at Leganes and went on to play for eight different lower-division clubs in Spain. He signed for Tenerife at the start of the 2025-26 season and scored 11 league goals in his first year, helping Tenerife win a long-awaited promotion to the Segunda Division.
At the start of the season, he attracted interest from Mohun Bagan SG. The former Indian Super League champions and among the biggest spenders in India were on the hunt for a top-notch striker following the departure of former Australian World Cupper Jason Cummings.
“We had a call with Jesus and his representative,” a senior Bagan official told TOI. “He said he was keen to come to India but there were two years remaining on his existing contract with Tenerife, so we could not make the transfer work. Jesus has scored consistently in the lower divisions in Spain and would have clicked in ISL.”
Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. They said on Tuesday that proceedings were opened and prosecutors will also be involved.
Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Pique, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga. “We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace,” Andorra said in a statement.
The Real Madrid players held a minute’s silence for De Miguel during training, while Espanyol postponed the presentation of their new coach.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy: Wadkar-Bhute tango takes Vidarbha to a first innings lead against Madhya Pradesh
briefs.bodyText:
Akshay Wadkar (100, 212b, 9x4) and Nachiket Bhute (97, 111, 6x4, 5x6) hauled Vidarbha to a first-innings lead on the second day of its Ranji Trophy Elite Group A match against Madhya Pradesh at the VCA Jamtha Stadium here.
Resuming on 56 for four, Vidarbha was pushed further back when it lost Dhruv Shorey and Harsh Dubey early in the first session. MP sensed an opportunity, but found itself repelled by Wadkar and Bhute’s counter-attack.
Bhute was the earlier aggressor, sending Saransh Jain and Kumar Kartikeya Singh to the fence repeatedly, while Wadkar manipulated the angles to find gaps in the field.
The duo soon brought the deficit below 100, and Nachiket launched Saransh for another straight six to bring up his half-century in 56 balls in the final over before Lunch.
Post resumption, the pair maintained a quick tempo against seamers Avesh and Ravi Kiran, capitalising on errant bowling, though Nachiket was fortunate to survive a pair of squandered opportunities.
The efficient Wadkar notched up his fifty from 122 balls before Bhute thrashed Kiran through the covers to confirm the host’s first-innings lead.
He reached his highest First-Class score with a six off Saransh but with three figures agonisingly close, MP brought Arshad Khan back and the 26-year-old fiddled behind.
Wadkar also struggled close to his century, and though he reached the milestone from 212 balls, it came at a heavy personal cost. He sealed his ton with a quick single, but injured himself diving and had to be stretchered off the field immediately afterwards.
Darshan Nalkande and Parth Rekhade managed to push Vidarbha’s lead beyond 100 before holing out off Saransh Jain, leaving MP with six overs to bat. However, it lost Yash Dubey just two balls in, leaving it facing a tall task again on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy: Pradosh, Ajith Ram pile more misery on Chandigarh
briefs.deck: The former registers a double ton while the latter brings up his maiden First Class hundred as the visitor declares its first innings at 571 for seven before reducing the host to 49 for three at close on day two
briefs.bodyText:
If Monday’s opening day was one of prayers being answered, Tuesday turned into a day of gifts for Tamil Nadu as Pradosh Ranjan Paul helped himself to a second First Class double hundred (208, 335b, 14x4), while Ajith Ram brought up his maiden First Class century (115 n.o., 219b, 10x4).
The duo piled on the agony for the host as the visitor declared its first innings at a mammoth 571 for seven on the second day of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash against Chandigarh at the Sector-16 Ground here on Tuesday.
The day began with overnight batter G. Ajitesh departing in just the second over of the morning as medium-pacer Rohit Dhanda breached his defence.
Thereafter, Pradosh and Ajith Ram took charge. The two initially took their time to settle down, showing patience and wearing down the bowlers before gradually opening up.
Once they found their rhythm, the runs began to flow. There were delightful square drives, crisp drives through the covers and pulls whenever the bowlers dropped short as the pair made the most of the scoring opportunities.
Pradosh reached his double hundred with a flick off a fuller-length delivery towards square-leg, letting out a roar before he was eventually castled by Chiragvir Dhindsa.
Ajith Ram then cut loose alongside skipper Sai Kishore, taking on the spinners and finding the boundaries with greater freedom.
He brought up his maiden three-figure mark with a boundary and yelled in delight, while Sai Kishore’s cameo (36 n.o., 35b, 2x4, 3x6) added to Chandigarh’s misery before TN declared.
In reply, Chandigarh finished the day at 49 for three in 20 overs, trailing by 522 runs.
